title: $\textit{MADFormer}$: Mixed Autoregressive and Diffusion Transformers for Continuous Image Generation
claim: A single unified Transformer with modality-specific parameters handles text autoregressively and images blockwise, splitting layers into condition-producing and denoising stages.
layout: Central Transformer bar, zoomed-in towers left and right, attention matrix at bottom center
description: A wide gray bar labeled Transformer runs across the top. A yellow dashed Text Tower sits at its left and a teal Image Tower at its right. Text tokens (An, old, man, '.') enter below the bar and shifted next tokens (old, man, '.', <EOT>) exit above. Image blocks, shown as face photos in teal dotted boxes, enter and leave through <BOI> tokens and the Image Tower. Dotted lines zoom the Text Tower into a yellow Decoder×N block. They also zoom the Image Tower into a teal stack: AR Module (Decoder×(N-D)), then Condition, then '+' with noisy patches, then Diffusion Module (Decoder×D). A lower-triangular gray blockwise causal attention matrix sits at the bottom center, linked to both towers. A legend marks the yellow (text) and teal (image) parameters.
caption: High-level overview of the MADFormer architecture. A single Transformer processes all modalities as a unified sequence. Text tokens follow a next-token prediction objective, while image tokens are grouped into blocks trained autoregressively with a diffusion objective. We use separate parameters (FFNs, QKVO projections, and layer norms) for each modality. The Transformer is divided into two stages: early layers produce conditions from text and image blocks; later layers denoise noisy image blocks. Each block attends to itself and preceding clean blocks. See Hu et al. [2024] for detailed attention patterns.
abstract: Recent progress in multimodal generation has increasingly combined autoregressive (AR) and diffusion-based approaches, leveraging their complementary strengths: AR models capture long-range dependencies and produce fluent, context-aware outputs, while diffusion models operate in continuous latent spaces to refine high-fidelity visual details. However, existing hybrids often lack systematic guidance on how and why to allocate model capacity between these paradigms. In this work, we introduce MADFormer, a Mixed Autoregressive and Diffusion Transformer that serves as a testbed for analyzing AR-diffusion trade-offs. MADFormer partitions image generation into spatial blocks, using AR layers for one-pass global conditioning across blocks and diffusion layers for iterative local refinement within each block. Through controlled experiments on FFHQ-1024 and ImageNet, we identify two key insights: (1) block-wise partitioning significantly improves performance on high-resolution images, and (2) vertically mixing AR and diffusion layers yields better quality-efficiency balances--improving FID by up to 75% under constrained inference compute. Our findings offer practical design principles for future hybrid generative models.
